title: bored and boring
rule: Adjectives in -ed describe how a person feels. Adjectives in -ing describe the thing that causes the feeling. I am bored. The film is boring. The same split works for interested/interesting, excited/exciting, tired/tiring.
ruleRu: -ed — что чувствует человек. -ing — что вызывает это чувство. I am bored. The film is boring. Так же interested/interesting и excited/exciting.
exampleOk: I was bored because the lesson was boring.
exampleBad: I was boring because the lesson was bored.
l1Trap: Оба переводят «скучный», и человек говорит I am boring, когда ему скучно.

title: how old
titleRu: Возраст: I am, не I have
rule: Age uses be, not have. I am 25. I am 25 years old. How old are you? Not I have 25 years.
ruleRu: Возраст — через be, не через have. I am 25. I am 25 years old. Не I have 25 years.
exampleOk: She is twenty years old.
exampleBad: She has twenty years.
l1Trap: Русское «мне двадцать лет» переводят как I have twenty years.

title: agree is a verb
rule: Agree is a verb. I agree. She agrees. I don't agree. Not I am agree and not I am agree with you. Agree with a person, agree on a plan, agree to a proposal.
ruleRu: Agree — глагол. I agree. She agrees. Не I am agree. Agree with — с человеком, agree on — о плане, agree to — на предложение.
exampleOk: I agree with you. We agreed on a price.
exampleBad: I am agree with you.
l1Trap: По образцу «я согласен» ставят am перед agree.

title: I like it very much
rule: Very goes before an adjective or adverb, not before a verb. I really like it. I like it very much. Not I very like it.
ruleRu: Very стоит перед прилагательным, не перед глаголом. I really like it. I like it very much. Не I very like it.
exampleOk: I really like this song.
exampleBad: I very like this song.
l1Trap: «Очень нравится» собирают как I very like.

title: feel, not feel myself
rule: For health and mood, feel takes an adjective and no reflexive. I feel tired. I feel well. Feel myself means to touch your own body.
ruleRu: Про самочувствие feel и прилагательное, без myself. I feel tired. I feel well. Feel myself — буквально трогать себя.
exampleOk: I feel ill today.
exampleBad: I feel myself ill today.
l1Trap: «Чувствую себя» переводят вместе с myself.

title: there, their, they're
rule: There is a place or there is/are. Their means belonging to them. They're means they are. Their car is there. They're late.
ruleRu: There — место или there is/are. Their — «их». They're = they are.
exampleOk: Their bags are over there. They're heavy.
exampleBad: They're bags are over their. There heavy.
l1Trap: Три слова звучат одинаково, и their пишут вместо there is.

title: your and you're
rule: Your shows possession. You're means you are. You're late. Is this your bag?
ruleRu: Your — «твой». You're = you are. You're late. Is this your bag?
exampleOk: You're right. Your answer is correct.
exampleBad: Your right. You're answer is correct.
l1Trap: Апостроф ставят на притяжательное your или забывают его в you are.

title: explain to someone
rule: Explain, describe and suggest do not take a person directly. Explain it to me. Describe it to her. Not explain me the rule.
ruleRu: После explain и describe человек идёт с to. Explain it to me. Не explain me.
exampleOk: Can you explain this rule to me?
exampleBad: Can you explain me this rule?
l1Trap: По русскому «объясни мне» ставят explain me.

title: ask someone to
rule: Ask and tell can take a person and to plus a verb. She asked me to wait. She told me to wait. Say cannot: not she said me to wait.
ruleRu: Ask и tell могут взять человека и to с глаголом. She asked me to wait. Say так не работает.
exampleOk: I asked her to call me.
exampleBad: I asked her calling me.
l1Trap: После ask ставят -ing или забывают to.

title: return, repeat, enter
titleRu: Return, repeat, enter без лишнего слова
rule: Return already means come back, so do not add back. Repeat already means say again. Enter a room, with no into. Discuss a topic, with no about.
ruleRu: Return уже значит «вернуться», back не нужно. Repeat уже значит «снова». Enter a room без into. Discuss a topic без about.
exampleOk: She returned home and entered the room.
exampleBad: She returned back home and entered into the room.
l1Trap: К этим глаголам прибавляют русские «обратно», «снова», «в».

title: call someone
rule: Call, phone and ring take a person with no to. Call me. I'll phone her later. Not call to me.
ruleRu: Call, phone и ring берут человека без to. Call me. Не call to me.
exampleOk: I'll call you tonight.
exampleBad: I'll call to you tonight.
l1Trap: «Позвонить кому-то» переводят с to.

title: by bus, on foot
rule: Use by with a means of transport and no article: by bus, by car, by train. The exception is on foot. Not by foot and not by the bus when you mean the means, not one particular bus.
ruleRu: Транспорт — by без артикля: by bus, by car. Пешком — on foot. Не by foot.
exampleOk: I go to work by bus. She came on foot.
exampleBad: I go to work by foot. She came by the bus.
l1Trap: Пешком говорят by foot, а перед bus ставят the.

title: languages without the
rule: Names of languages have no article. She speaks Russian. A lesson in English. Use the only when the word means the people: the English, the Russians.
ruleRu: Названия языков без артикля. She speaks Russian. The English — это англичане, не язык.
exampleOk: I'm learning English.
exampleBad: I'm learning the English.
l1Trap: Перед языком ставят the, как перед названием народа.

title: days and months
titleRu: Дни и месяцы с большой буквы
rule: Days and months start with a capital letter. Monday, January. Seasons do not, unless they start a sentence: summer, winter. On Monday. In January.
ruleRu: Дни и месяцы пишутся с большой буквы: Monday, January. Времена года — нет: summer. On Monday. In January.
exampleOk: We met on Monday in January.
exampleBad: We met on monday in january.
l1Trap: В русском дни и месяцы со строчной, и это переносят в английский.

title: saying the date
rule: Use on with a date. Write 5 May or May 5. Say the fifth of May or May the fifth. Not on 5th May with a written ordinal if you are following the simple written form, and not in 5 May.
ruleRu: С датой — on. Пишут 5 May или May 5. Говорят the fifth of May. Не in 5 May.
exampleOk: The meeting is on 5 May.
exampleBad: The meeting is in 5 May.
l1Trap: Дату ставят с in, как русское «в мае» и «пятого».

title: telling the time
rule: Half past six is 6:30. Quarter past six is 6:15. Quarter to seven is 6:45. Say the hour after the minutes with past and to. Not half to six for 6:30.
ruleRu: Half past six — 6:30. Quarter past — пятнадцать минут следующего часа. Quarter to seven — без пятнадцати семь. Не half to six.
exampleOk: It's half past six.
exampleBad: It's half to six.
l1Trap: «Половина седьмого» переводят как half past seven или half to six.

title: how much and how many
rule: How many is for countable plurals. How much is for uncountables and for price. How many books? How much time? How much is it?
ruleRu: How many — штуки. How much — масса, время и цена. How many books? How much is it?
exampleOk: How many tickets do we need? How much are they?
exampleBad: How much tickets do we need?
l1Trap: How much ставят и перед считаемыми, потому что «сколько» одно.

title: what and which
rule: What asks about an open set. Which asks about a small known set. What music do you like? Which of these two songs do you prefer?
ruleRu: What — открытый выбор. Which — из уже известного короткого списка. Which of these two?
exampleOk: Which of these bags is yours?
exampleBad: What of these bags is yours?
l1Trap: What ставят и когда выбор из двух-трёх вещей на столе.

title: too ... to
rule: Too plus adjective plus to plus verb means the degree stops the action. Too tired to drive. Not too tired for drive and not enough tired.
ruleRu: Too, прилагательное и to с глаголом — степень мешает действию. Too tired to drive.
exampleOk: It was too cold to swim.
exampleBad: It was too cold for swim.
l1Trap: После too ставят for и начальную форму вместо to.

title: to, in order to, for
rule: Purpose with a verb is to or in order to. Purpose with a noun is for. I came to ask. This knife is for bread. Not for to ask and not for ask.
ruleRu: Цель с глаголом — to или in order to. Цель с существительным — for. Не for to ask.
exampleOk: She stopped to buy bread.
exampleBad: She stopped for to buy bread.
l1Trap: Цель собирают как for to, по французскому или по «для того чтобы».

title: so that
rule: So that introduces a purpose clause and usually has can, could, will or would. She spoke slowly so that we could understand. Not so that to understand.
ruleRu: So that вводит цель и обычно идёт с can, could, will или would. Не so that to.
exampleOk: I left early so that I would be on time.
exampleBad: I left early so that to be on time.
l1Trap: После so that ставят to и инфинитив, как после in order.

title: it is important to
rule: Use it as an empty subject before an adjective and to plus a verb. It is important to rest. It is easy to say. Not Is important to rest and not It is important resting.
ruleRu: Перед прилагательным и to нужен пустой it. It is important to rest. Не Is important и не important resting.
exampleOk: It is hard to hear you.
exampleBad: Is hard to hear you.
l1Trap: It выбрасывают, потому что в русском подлежащего нет.

title: look for, look after, look at
titleRu: Look for, look after, look at
rule: Look for means try to find. Look after means take care of. Look at means turn your eyes to. Look forward to takes -ing. They are not interchangeable.
ruleRu: Look for — искать. Look after — присматривать. Look at — смотреть на. Look forward to требует -ing.
exampleOk: I'm looking for my keys. Can you look after the baby?
exampleBad: I'm looking after my keys. Can you look for the baby today?
l1Trap: Все look переводят «смотреть» и предлоги меняют.

title: give up
rule: Give up plus a noun or verb-ing means stop a habit. Give up smoking. A pronoun goes in the middle: give it up. Not give up it.
ruleRu: Give up и существительное или -ing — бросить привычку. Местоимение ставится в середину: give it up.
exampleOk: She gave up sugar. She gave it up in January.
exampleBad: She gave up it in January.
l1Trap: Местоимение оставляют после частицы: give up it.

title: turn on and turn off
rule: Turn on and turn off take a device. A pronoun goes in the middle: turn it off. Not close the light and not turn off it.
ruleRu: Turn on и turn off — про прибор. Местоимение в середине: turn it off. Не close the light.
exampleOk: Please turn the light off. Turn it on again later.
exampleBad: Please close the light. Turn off it.
l1Trap: Свет «закрывают», как дверь, и говорят close the light.

title: either or, neither nor
rule: Either ... or joins two possibilities. Neither ... nor joins two negatives and needs no extra not. Neither the bus nor the train was running. The verb usually agrees with the nearer noun.
ruleRu: Either ... or — один из двух. Neither ... nor — ни то ни другое, второе not не нужно.
exampleOk: Neither Anna nor her brother was at home.
exampleBad: Neither Anna or her brother were not at home.
l1Trap: Or ставят после neither и добавляют ещё одно отрицание.

title: not only but also
rule: Not only and but also are a pair. She speaks not only English but also French. Do not drop also, and do not write not only ... but too.
ruleRu: Not only и but also идут парой. Не not only ... but too.
exampleOk: He not only cooks but also bakes.
exampleBad: He not only cooks but bakes too.
l1Trap: Вторую часть закрывают через too, как русское «а ещё».

title: belong to, consist of
rule: Belong takes to. Consist takes of. It belongs to me. The group consists of six people. Not belong me and not consist from.
ruleRu: Belong требует to. Consist требует of. Не consist from.
exampleOk: This bag belongs to Anna. The team consists of five players.
exampleBad: This bag belongs Anna. The team consists from five players.
l1Trap: From и отсутствие предлога идут из «принадлежит» и «состоит из».

title: apologise, thank, congratulate
rule: Apologise to a person for a thing. Thank a person for a thing. Congratulate a person on a thing. The verb after the preposition is -ing. Thank you for coming. Not apologise about and not congratulate for.
ruleRu: Apologise to someone for something. Thank someone for. Congratulate someone on. После предлога глагол с -ing.
exampleOk: She apologised to me for being late.
exampleBad: She apologised me about being late.
l1Trap: Предлоги about и for ставят не к тем глаголам, и to после apologise теряют.

title: opportunity and possibility
rule: An opportunity is a good chance for a person to do something. A possibility is whether something can happen at all. I had the opportunity to speak. There is a possibility of rain. Not a possibility to speak when you mean a chance you were given.
ruleRu: Opportunity — удачный шанс для человека что-то сделать. Possibility — может ли это вообще случиться.
exampleOk: I had an opportunity to travel. There is a possibility of snow.
exampleBad: I had a possibility to travel.
l1Trap: Оба читают как «возможность», и possibility ставят про личный шанс.

title: convenient and comfortable
rule: Convenient means suitable, easy for a plan: a convenient time. Comfortable means physically pleasant: a comfortable chair. Not a convenient chair.
ruleRu: Convenient — подходящий по времени и плану. Comfortable — физически удобный. Не a convenient chair.
exampleOk: Is Saturday a convenient day? This chair is comfortable.
exampleBad: This chair is very convenient.
l1Trap: Convenient читают как «удобный» про мебель и одежду.

title: check, not control
rule: Check means look to see if something is right. Control means direct or limit. Check your answers. Control a machine. Not control your homework when you mean mark it.
ruleRu: Check — проверить, всё ли верно. Control — управлять или сдерживать. Домашнюю работу check, не control.
exampleOk: The teacher checked our tests.
exampleBad: The teacher controlled our tests.
l1Trap: Control читают как «контролировать, проверять».

title: intelligent and educated
rule: Intelligent means clever, quick to understand. Educated, cultured or well-read is closer to a person of wide culture. She is intelligent. He is well-read.
ruleRu: Intelligent — умный, сообразительный. «Интеллигентный» ближе к educated, cultured, well-read.
exampleOk: She is intelligent and well-read.
exampleBad: She is a very intelligent person in the sense of good manners only.
l1Trap: Intelligent ставят про манеры и начитанность.

title: artist and actor
rule: An artist makes pictures or other art. An actor acts in films and plays. A musician plays music. Not an artist of the theatre when you mean an actor.
ruleRu: Artist — художник. Actor — актёр. Musician — музыкант.
exampleOk: The actor thanked the artist who painted the set.
exampleBad: The theatre artist forgot his lines.
l1Trap: Artist читают как «артист».

title: novel and new
rule: A novel is a long book of fiction. New means not old. A novel idea means an original idea, which is a different use. Not a novel car for a new car.
ruleRu: A novel — роман. New — новый. Novel idea — оригинальная мысль, не «новая машина».
exampleOk: She wrote a novel about a new city.
exampleBad: She bought a novel car.
l1Trap: Novel читают как «новый».

title: economic and economical
rule: Economic is about the economy or money at a large scale: economic growth. Economical means not wasteful: an economical car. Historic is important in history. Historical is about the past, whether important or not.
ruleRu: Economic — про экономику. Economical — бережливый, не расточительный. Historic — исторически важный. Historical — относящийся к прошлому.
exampleOk: Economic growth slowed. This car is economical.
exampleBad: This car is very economic to run.
l1Trap: Пары на -ic и -ical читают как одно слово.

title: beside and besides
rule: Beside means next to. Besides means in addition or except. Sit beside me. Besides English, she speaks French.
ruleRu: Beside — рядом. Besides — кроме того или кроме. Sit beside me. Besides English, she speaks French.
exampleOk: Besides tea, we have coffee.
exampleBad: Beside tea, we have coffee.
l1Trap: Оба читают как «кроме» или как «рядом».

title: rise and raise
rule: Rise does not take an object: prices rise, the sun rises. Raise takes an object: raise your hand, raise prices, raise a child. The past of rise is rose, risen. The past of raise is raised.
ruleRu: Rise — без дополнения: prices rise. Raise — с дополнением: raise your hand. Прошедшее от rise — rose.
exampleOk: Prices rose, so the shop raised its prices.
exampleBad: Prices raised, so the shop rose its prices.
l1Trap: Оба значат «поднимать(ся)», и формы путают.

title: steal and rob
rule: Steal a thing from a person or place. Rob a person or place of a thing. Someone stole my bag. Someone robbed the bank. Not stole me and not robbed my bag.
ruleRu: Steal — украсть вещь. Rob — ограбить человека или место. Stole my bag. Robbed the bank.
exampleOk: They stole her phone. They robbed the shop.
exampleBad: They robbed her phone. They stole the shop.
l1Trap: Оба переводят «украсть», и дополнения меняют местами.

title: miss and lose
rule: Lose means you cannot find something or you are defeated. Miss means you arrive too late, or you feel sad because someone is away. I lost my keys. I missed the train. I miss you.
ruleRu: Lose — потерять вещь или проиграть. Miss — опоздать на транспорт или скучать. I lost my keys. I missed the train. I miss you.
exampleOk: I missed the bus and lost my ticket.
exampleBad: I lost the bus and missed my ticket on the floor.
l1Trap: Lose the bus говорят вместо missed the bus.

title: forget and leave
rule: Leave a thing in a place. Forget a thing, with no place, or forget to do something. I left my bag at home. I forgot my bag. Not I forgot my bag at home.
ruleRu: Leave — оставить в месте. Forget — забыть, без места, или забыть сделать. I left my bag at home. Не I forgot my bag at home.
exampleOk: I left the keys in the car. I forgot to lock it.
exampleBad: I forgot the keys in the car.
l1Trap: Forgot ставят с местом, как русское «забыл в машине».

title: price and cost
rule: Price is the noun for the amount on a label. Cost is the verb, and also the noun for what you spend. How much does it cost? The price is high. Not How much does it price?
ruleRu: Price — цена на ценнике, существительное. Cost — глагол «стоить» и существительное «затраты». How much does it cost?
exampleOk: The price is 20 pounds. It costs 20 pounds.
exampleBad: It prices 20 pounds.
l1Trap: Price используют как глагол «стоить».

title: meet and know
rule: Meet is the first time or an arrangement. Know is the state after that. I met her in 2019. I have known her since 2019. Nice to meet you is only the first time. Later say nice to see you.
ruleRu: Meet — познакомиться или встретиться по договорённости. Know — знать после этого. В первый раз — Nice to meet you. Потом — Nice to see you.
exampleOk: We met last year, so I know her. Nice to see you again.
exampleBad: Nice to meet you again. I met her since 2019.
l1Trap: Nice to meet you говорят при каждой встрече, а know заменяют на meet.

title: let's
rule: Let's plus the base verb is a suggestion that includes the speaker. Let's go. The negative is let's not. Not let's to go and not let's don't go.
ruleRu: Let's и глагол без to — предложение, в которое входит говорящий. Let's go. Отрицание — let's not.
exampleOk: Let's not wait.
exampleBad: Let's don't wait.
l1Trap: После let's ставят to или don't.

title: was going to
rule: Was or were going to is a plan in the past, often one that did not happen. I was going to call you, but I forgot. Not I was going call.
ruleRu: Was/were going to — план в прошлом, часто несостоявшийся. I was going to call you, but I forgot.
exampleOk: We were going to walk, but it rained.
exampleBad: We were going walk, but it rained.
l1Trap: To после going теряют, как в разговорном gonna, но в учебной фразе его нет.

title: be about to
rule: Be about to plus the base verb means the action is going to happen in a moment. The train is about to leave. Not The train is about leaving.
ruleRu: Be about to и глагол — действие вот-вот начнётся. The train is about to leave.
exampleOk: Sit down. The film is about to start.
exampleBad: The film is about starting.
l1Trap: После about ставят -ing, как после предлога.

title: however
rule: However contrasts two sentences. It usually starts the second sentence and is followed by a comma. It was late. However, we stayed. Not It was late however we stayed, as if however were but.
ruleRu: However противопоставляет два предложения и обычно стоит в начале второго, с запятой. Это не замена but внутри одной связи.
exampleOk: The hotel was expensive. However, the room was quiet.
exampleBad: The hotel was expensive however the room was quiet.
l1Trap: However ставят вместо but без точки и запятой.

title: according to
rule: According to introduces a source. According to the map, we turn left. Do not use according to me for your own opinion. Say in my opinion.
ruleRu: According to называет источник. According to the map. Про своё мнение — in my opinion, не according to me.
exampleOk: According to Anna, the shop is closed. In my opinion, we should check.
exampleBad: According to me, the shop is closed.
l1Trap: According to me говорят вместо «по-моему».

title: instead of
rule: Instead of takes a noun or verb-ing. We walked instead of taking the bus. Instead, without of, can start a clause: We didn't take the bus. Instead, we walked.
ruleRu: Instead of и существительное или -ing. Instead без of начинает отдельную фразу.
exampleOk: Instead of driving, we walked.
exampleBad: Instead of to drive, we walked.
l1Trap: После instead of ставят to и инфинитив.

title: all and the whole
rule: The whole takes a singular noun and usually the: the whole day. All can take a plural or uncountable: all day, all the students. Not the all day and not whole the students.
ruleRu: The whole — одно целое: the whole day. All — со множественным или без артикля: all day, all the students.
exampleOk: I spent the whole day at home. All the shops were shut.
exampleBad: I spent the all day at home.
l1Trap: All и whole меняют местами и ставят the all.

title: most of
rule: Most plus a plural means the majority in general: most people. Most of needs the, a pronoun or a specific group: most of the people, most of them. The verb after most of them is plural.
ruleRu: Most people — большинство вообще. Most of the people или most of them — из конкретной группы. Глагол после them во множественном.
exampleOk: Most of the students were late. Most people walk.
exampleBad: Most of students was late.
l1Trap: The после most of теряют, и глагол ставят в единственном.
